title: Decode a Base64 string into an image

seo.metaTitle: Base64 to PNG - Free Browser Decoder, Nothing Is Uploaded
seo.metaDescription: Paste a Base64 string or a data URI and get the picture back, ready to download. Free, no upload, no account - the decoding happens right in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Decode a Base64 string turns the text back into the image bytes it was made from — the PNG to Base64 encoder run backwards. Paste the string, the bytes are decoded in your browser and the picture appears beside the text field; whitespace and line breaks are ignored, and a complete data: URI works as well as the bare payload because the prefix is stripped first. What comes back is the picture, not the original file: the bytes are decoded to pixels and encoded again, so every pixel is identical while the file bytes are not guaranteed to match. Nothing is uploaded — pasted Base64 is often a credential rather than a photo.
facts: Decoding runs entirely in your browser: nothing is sent to a server.
Accepts the bare payload or a full data: URI; whitespace and line breaks are ignored.
Reads whatever format the bytes describe — JPG and WebP payloads decode too.
The pixels match the original; the file bytes are not guaranteed to.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Copy the Base64 string and paste it into the text field on the left; a full data: URI works too.
The decoded picture appears in the result tile on the right.
Save it from the Download button, as PNG or in another format.

faq.q: Do I need the MIME type or the file name?
faq.a: Neither. Paste the payload alone and it is decoded as it is; paste the whole data:image/png;base64,... value and the prefix is removed first. The PNG signature check on this site reads the first bytes if you want a yes or no before decoding.

faq.q: Why is the downloaded file not identical to my original?
faq.a: The string holds compressed bytes while the picture you see is decoded pixels, and saving encodes those pixels again. The pixels match; the bytes are not promised to.

faq.q: Will it decode a Base64 string of a JPG or a WebP?
faq.a: Yes. The decoder reads whatever format the bytes describe, so a JPG payload gives back the JPG picture. You can still save it as PNG.

faq.q: Is my pasted string sent to a server?
faq.a: No. It is decoded and discarded in your browser tab, and the page makes no request with it - which matters when the string is a secret rather than a picture.
